public_rationale: Anthropic's standard terms in force on March 31, 2026 allowed feature changes and capacity reductions, subject to separately agreed terms [e1]. OpenAI's terms in force that day allowed service changes and required at least 30 days' notice for materially adverse changes to the terms [e2]. These provisions supplied no three-month assurance that an ordinary subscriber's existing workload would remain supported unchanged through June 30, 2026 [e1, e2].
limitations: The terms do not establish practical predictability for any particular workload or whether it later became unsupported [e1, e2].
The cited standard terms do not establish the protections in separately negotiated agreements [e1, e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Claude Code and Codex subscribers cannot know whether their current workloads will still be supported in three months.

statement.excerpt: A Claude Code or OpenAI Codex user cannot with any clarity say that in three months their current workload or workflow will be possible based on their current subscription.
statement.document_title: The Subprime AI Crisis Is Here

from_speaker: A Claude Code or OpenAI Codex user
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading concerns reliable assurance supplied by a standard subscription, rather than a prediction that every user's workflow will actually fail.
Assess the terms in force on March 31, 2026, and whether they assure unchanged workload support through June 30, 2026.
The scope is ordinary individual subscriptions. Separately negotiated enterprise guarantees require separate examination.
Three months describes the assurance being discussed; it does not turn the statement into a forecast of actual service failure.
criteria.support_condition: Both providers' standard terms allow relevant service or capacity changes within three months and do not assure unchanged support for a subscriber's existing workload throughout that interval.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The relevant standard subscriptions provide enforceable three-month assurances of the capacity and functionality needed to continue existing workloads.
